comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C6, C46-C50 regarding Scc1 restoration after DSBs in telophase. Both evaluations find this supported by Western blot data in Figure 1B-E. All three peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as compelling and convincing evidence.

Perfect agreement on claims C105-C109 being speculative. Both evaluations rate these as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these are 'explicitly speculative' hypotheses requiring future validation. Peer Reviewer 3 identifies the disconnect between cohesin reconstitution and functional role in HR, requesting clarification that this remains speculative.

Strong agreement on claims C7, C51-C55 regarding Scc1 co-precipitation with Smc1-HA and acSmc3. OpenEval finds this supported by co-IP data in Figure 2A. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge Scc1 reassociation with Smc1-3 subunits as convincingly established, with no concerns raised.

Agreement on claims C56-C58 regarding chromatin-bound cohesin complex. OpenEval finds this supported by chromatin fractionation data in Figure 2B. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the broader finding that Scc1 reassociates with chromatin and other cohesin subunits.

Agreement on claims C9, C61-C63 regarding lack of local cohesin recruitment to DSB site in telophase. OpenEval finds this supported by ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 2C. Peer reviewers accept this finding, with Reviewer 3 noting it is consistent with cohesin playing no role in this specific HR context.

Strong agreement on claims C80-C83, C87, C103-C104 regarding efficient HR in telophase. Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED by Southern blot data in Figure 3E-F. All peer reviewers explicitly confirm HR occurs efficiently in telophase-arrested cells as convincingly established, with the editor noting this as a key finding.

Agreement on claims C8, C100-C101 regarding cohesin dispensability for MAT switching HR. OpenEval finds claim C100 supported by quantification in Figure 4D showing no significant differences. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as one of three facts convincingly established, with Reviewer 3 stating cohesin plays no role in this specific HR context.

Agreement on claims C68-C71 regarding resection kinetics in telophase. OpenEval finds this supported by qPCR data in Figure 3A. Peer reviewers accept this data as part of evidence that HR machinery is functional in telophase, with Reviewer 1 acknowledging careful cell synchronization and repair monitoring.

Agreement on claims C74, C79 regarding Rad53 activation and checkpoint response. OpenEval finds this supported by Western blot data in Figures 3B and 3D. Peer reviewers accept checkpoint activation data as supporting HR functionality in telophase without challenge.

Agreement on claims C84-C85 regarding similar repair kinetics in mutants. OpenEval finds this supported by data in Figure 3-supplement 2D-I. Peer reviewers accept these findings as supporting evidence for robustness of HR in telophase, consistent with established MAT switching knowledge.

OpenEval evaluates 33 background and context claims (C1-C5, C10-C33, C37-C40, C42) as SUPPORTED by appropriate literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers typically focus on novel findings rather than background claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C34-C36, C41, C43 as SUPPORTED, including the hypothesis that cohesin reconstitution is feasible (C41) based on established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background and hypothesis claims.

OpenEval rates claims C59-C60, C64-C66 as UNCERTAIN, noting these are explicitly speculative hypotheses about mechanisms ('could be due to', 'might act', 'may shift') that remain untested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mechanistic speculations.
